# Research report 1 of 2

## AI solves a Millennium Prize Problem in September 2026: research notes (as of 2026-09-08)

The main finding: on September 8, OpenAI announced that its AI system had solved the Navier-Stokes problem. That likely bears directly on resolution, but it is a claim that hasn't been verified, and there are open questions about whether it matches the official problem statement and who deserves credit. Page fetches were blocked, so most of the details below come from search-result summaries, not from reading the articles. The exact time of the announcement on Sept 8 relative to the 04:31 UTC close is also unclear.

### 1. Resolution source
- The criteria point to the Wikipedia "Millennium Prize Problems" page. I couldn't load it. A search summary of the page says the Poincaré conjecture is still the only problem officially declared solved, mentions OpenAI's Navier-Stokes claim, and says the claim had not been independently verified. I can't confirm the date of the version that was summarized. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millennium_Prize_Problems)
- The market creator clarified on 2026-09-04 that a valid solution announced in September resolves YES, even if the work was done earlier.

### 2. Current status
- 2026-09-08: OpenAI published "On the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize Problem." It says an internal multi-agent system (around 10,000 concurrent agents) produced a proof and a Lean formalization showing that a smooth fluid starting at rest can develop a singularity in finite time, i.e., blowup. It says it does not intend to claim the $1M prize. [OpenAI](https://openai.com/index/navier-stokes-solution/)
- OpenAI says the agents reached the result on Saturday 2026-09-05, about 88 hours after launch, and Lean verification took about 17 more hours. It says the work started 2026-09-01 after a "rumor" that another Millennium problem was being solved. [OpenAI](https://openai.com/index/navier-stokes-solution/); [Axios](https://www.axios.com/2026/09/08/openai-math-solution-navier-stokes-credit)
- 2026-09-08: Quanta ran the headline "AI Has Solved One of Math's $1 Million Millennium Prize Problems." According to secondary reports, it says the Lean proof gives strong confidence that the logic holds together, but experts still have to check that the formal statement matches the Clay formulation. [Quanta](https://www.quantamagazine.org/ai-has-solved-one-of-maths-1-million-millennium-prize-problems-20260908/)
- Main caveats:
  - One summary says the proof covers the *forced* version of the equations, not the unforced one. Note that the official Clay problem statement includes "breakdown" options that allow a forcing term, so a forced result could still qualify. Whether this one does is undecided. [NYU Shanghai RITS](https://rits.shanghai.nyu.edu/ai/openai-navier-stokes-proof-credit-dispute/)
  - The Clay Mathematics Institute has not commented, and there has been no peer review. [Axios](https://www.axios.com/2026/09/08/openai-math-solution-navier-stokes-credit)
  - Credit dispute: on 2026-09-07, mathematicians Tristan Buckmaster (NYU) and Levent Alpöge (Anthropic) released Lean-verified blowup proofs for related fluid equations, and they say they were working on Navier-Stokes themselves with help from LLMs. That raises a question for the "substantial work done by AI" and "not already solved by humans" criteria. [MIT Tech Review](https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/09/08/1143747/what-openais-latest-controversy-tells-us-about-the-future-of-math/)

### 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-09-08: Axios reports the announcement is "overshadowed by credit controversy." [Axios](https://www.axios.com/2026/09/08/openai-math-solution-navier-stokes-credit)
- 2026-09-08: MIT Technology Review notes that Buckmaster posted on Mastodon a proof of breakdown for a simplified version of Navier-Stokes. [MIT Tech Review](https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/09/08/1143747/what-openais-latest-controversy-tells-us-about-the-future-of-math/)
- 2026-09-08: Simon Willison blog post, "Some thoughts on the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize Problem." [Simon Willison](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Sep/8/on-navier-stokes/)
- 2026-09-05: Terence Tao reportedly gave a warning about this kind of race, before OpenAI's announcement. I couldn't find what he said. [NYU Shanghai RITS](https://rits.shanghai.nyu.edu/ai/openai-navier-stokes-proof-credit-dispute/)
- About 2026-08-15: Buckmaster and Alpöge (with Coiculescu) reportedly announced finite-time blowup for 3D incompressible Euler with smooth forcing, using heavy LLM help. Tao reportedly said the method might extend to Navier-Stokes. This comes from a single, uncorroborated alert. [aiweekly.co](https://aiweekly.co/fr/alerts/buckmaster-nyu-accuse-openai-dappropriation-sur-navier-stokes); [bubbles.town](https://bubbles.town/entry/44781468)

### 4. Base rates
- Since the prizes were announced in 2000, only one problem has been solved: Poincaré (Perelman, 2002-03, recognized in 2010). No AI had ever been credited with solving one before this claim. That works out to roughly 1 human solution in about 26 years, and 0 by AI before September 2026. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millennium_Prize_Problems)
- Clay's own rules require publication plus a two-year waiting period before any award. That doesn't decide this market, which turns on an "announcement" of a "valid solution."

### 5. Other forecasts
- 2026-09-05: A Manifold contract on AI solving a Millennium problem in 2026 was reportedly at about 38% YES. [tech-insider](https://tech-insider.org/ai-solve-important-math-conjecture-2030-manifold-odds/)

# Research report 2 of 2 (written independently)

I've finished the searches and am writing up what was published on or before 2026-09-08. A few fetches were blocked, and many results were dated after the cutoff. I left those out.

## 1. Resolution source
- The criteria cite the Wikipedia page "Millennium Prize Problems". I couldn't fetch it because the proxy refused the connection, so I can't report what it showed on 2026-09-08. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millennium_Prize_Problems)
- Long-standing status: of the seven problems, only the Poincaré conjecture is solved, by Perelman. Navier-Stokes is still listed as open on Clay's side. [Kingy AI overview](https://kingy.ai/millennium-prize-problems-ai/)
- 2026-08-21: one explainer said no Millennium Prize Problem had a published, peer-reviewed proof from either AI or humans as of that date. [explainx.ai](https://explainx.ai/blog/millennium-prize-problems-ai-solved-fact-check-2026)

## 2. Current status
- 2026-09-08 (a Tuesday): several outlets report that OpenAI announced an internal, unreleased AI system had produced a proof. They say it shows that smooth, forced 3D Navier-Stokes flow can blow up in finite time, which would be a counterexample. The proof reportedly comes with a Lean formalization and was produced in about 88 hours by up to 10,000 parallel agents. [OpenAI post](https://openai.com/index/navier-stokes-solution/), [Unite.AI](https://www.unite.ai/?p=463595), [Let's Data Science](https://letsdatascience.com/news/openai-publishes-proposed-navier-stokes-singularity-proof-83719c42)
- I couldn't fetch OpenAI's page or find the time of day of the announcement. It may have come after forecasts closed at 04:31 UTC on 9/8.
- What was known by 9/8: this is a company claim. It has not been peer-reviewed, and there is no Clay recognition. Reportedly OpenAI does not intend to claim the prize. A Lean check verifies only the formal statement that was entered, so experts still have to judge whether it matches Clay's exact problem. One commentary argues it covers only the forced-case variants (C/D) of the Clay statement. Whether that counts as "solved" for Wikipedia and this market's creator is the key open question.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-09-08: OpenAI's Navier-Stokes announcement (above). Reports say OpenAI started the effort on 2026-09-01 after hearing a rumor that another Millennium problem was being resolved. [Let's Data Science](https://letsdatascience.com/news/openai-claims-navier-stokes-millennium-problem-solution-97e934f2)
- 2026-09-07 (or 2026-08-15; sources conflict): Tristan Buckmaster (NYU) and Levent Alpöge (an Anthropic-employed mathematician) announced finite-time blowup for 3D Euler with smooth forcing (zero viscosity). This is a step toward Navier-Stokes but not the Millennium problem itself. It was human-led with heavy LLM iteration, and the ideas are credited partly to Córdoba and Martínez-Zoroa. [aiweekly (FR)](https://aiweekly.co/fr/alerts/buckmaster-nyu-accuse-openai-dappropriation-sur-navier-stokes), [bubbles.town](https://bubbles.town/entry/44781468)
- 2026-09-04: the question creator clarified that the market resolves on an announcement made in September, even if the work was done earlier.
- 2026-05: an arXiv preprint on asymptotically self-similar blowup for 3D Euler shows this research area was very active. [arXiv 2605.15149](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2605.15149)
- Earlier: Google DeepMind used physics-informed neural networks to find new families of unstable singularities in fluid equations. A February preprint argued that axisymmetric Euler blowups likely don't carry over to Navier-Stokes. [Decrypt](https://decrypt.co/340451/google-deepmind-ai-cracks-century-old-fluid-mysteries-new-era-science), [Scientific American](https://scientificamerican.com/article/humans-and-ai-race-to-blow-up-maths-toughest-equations)

## 4. Base rates
- In 26 years (2000 to 2026), one of seven problems was solved (Poincaré, 2002-03), entirely by a human. That's about 1 solution in roughly 300 problem-months.
- Before September 2026 I found no AI-led resolution of any Millennium problem. The base rate for any single month is close to zero. The September 2026 Navier-Stokes activity breaks sharply from that pattern.

## 5. Other forecasts
- 2026-09-05: a secondary article says a Manifold market "AI solves Millennium Prize Problem in 2026?" was at 38%. That is the full-year version, not this September one, and the page is unverified because my fetch failed. [tech-insider](https://tech-insider.org/?p=20283)
- Related Manifold markets (snapshot dates unclear): "another Millennium problem solved in 2026" at about 57%, and "AI solves another Millennium problem by end of 2027" at about 22%. [Manifold event](https://manifold.markets/event/will-an-ai-solve-a-millennium-probl), [Manifold: another](https://manifold.markets/LavrovAndrey/will-ai-solve-another-millennium-pr), [Manifold: will another](https://manifold.markets/HumanClanker/will-another-millennium-prize-probl)

- Another Manifold market asks whether OpenAI will publicly claim a solution. [Manifold](https://manifold.markets/Terminator2/will-openai-publicly-claim-a-soluti)
- I couldn't find this September market's own price.

## 6. Upcoming events that could move the outcome
- How the creator reads OpenAI's 9/8 announcement: whether a forced-case counterexample with a Lean proof counts as "solved," and whether it counts as AI doing the substantial work.
- Whether the Wikipedia page gets updated, and expert or Clay reactions.
